item.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
item.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.

item.title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters. According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9. He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers. Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.” The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state. The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process. Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state. He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise. “The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections. “The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added. He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. Vanguard News The post REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UH quarterback Conner Weigman ruled out for Cougars' game at West VIrginia
item.description: Conner Weigman, who was banged up last week at Colorado, showed up on the injury report Friday night before being ruled out Saturday. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - University of Houston quarterback Conner Weigman is out for Saturday's game against West Virginia. Weigman has been dealing with a right shoulder injury he suffered Nov. 13 at Colorado. Weigman has thrown for 2,552 yards and 25 touchdowns and has a team-high seven rushing touchdowns for the No. 20 Cougars, who are 7-3 entering the final two weeks of the regular season. Keisean Henderson will start in Weigman's place. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: BYU teams finish in top 4 at NCAA cross country championships
item.description: BYU's Jane Hedengren competes at the Big 12 Championship in Stillwater, Okla. Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. Hedengren won her second consecutive individual Big 12 Women's Championship title with a time of 19:28.0. | Emma Thomas/BYU Photo No. 1 became third. No. 6 became fourth. That was BYU’s day at the NCAA cross country championships Saturday at the Lavern Gibson Cross Country Course in Terre Haute, Indiana. The BYU women stood on the podium. The men finished fourth, one point ahead of Oregon. The titles went to Alabama (women) and New Mexico (men). The Cougars entered the meet in the conversation but finished short of a champions trophy. No. 4-ranked Alabama won its first women’s team title with 120 points. No. 3 West Virginia took second with 145. Diljeet Taylor’s Cougars, the Big 12 champions and the No. 1 team in the country, scored 152, good for third. It was a slip of sorts. A year ago they finished second to NC State. Two years ago they won it all. They were chasing a third national championship since 2020, and a seventh in program history. They did not get it. Alabama ended a stretch in which every women’s title since 2020 had belonged to BYU or NC State. NC State’s Hannah Gapes won the individual 6-kilometer race in 18:44.3, breaking her own course record. South Carolina’s Salma Elbadra was second in 18:51.8. BYU’s punch came in a pack, not at the front. Senior Lexi Goff-Thompson led the Cougars in 26th in 19:18.5. Senior Taylor Lovell was 27th in 19:19.5. Senior Riley Chamberlain, in her first and only cross country race of the season, placed 35th in 19:24.3. Sophomore Jane Hedengren, last year’s national runner-up and the Big 12 individual champion, finished 39th in 19:26.1. Senior Taylor Rohatinsky was the fifth scorer in 59th in 19:37.6. Hedengren, among the top runners in the nation, had struggled lately with some health issues and was questionable if she would compete leading into this title race. The top 40 earn All-America honors. That made All-Americans of Goff-Thompson, Lovell, Chamberlain and Hedengren. After questions about whether she would start, Hedengren was about 40th through the first kilometer, according to FloTrack, and finished just inside that line. Then the men. Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto won the 10-kilometer race in 28:27.7, a course record. Alabama’s Dismus Lokira was second in 28:30.8. Oklahoma State’s Denis Kipngetich took third in 28:32.5. No. 1 New Mexico won the team title with 69 points. No. 2 Colorado was second with 107. No. 4 Alabama took the last podium spot with 109. No. 6 BYU was fourth with 195, one point ahead of No. 5 Oregon. Ed Eyestone had almost drawn that map before the gun. Hedengren won her second consecutive individual Big 12 Women's Championship title with a time of 19:28.0. | Emma Thomas/BYU Photo No. 1 became third. No. 6 became fourth. That was BYU’s day at the NCAA cross country championships Saturday at the Lavern Gibson Cross Country Course in Terre Haute, Indiana. The BYU women stood on the podium. The men finished fourth, one point ahead of Oregon. The titles went to Alabama (women) and New Mexico (men). The Cougars entered the meet in the conversation but finished short of a champions trophy. No. 4-ranked Alabama won its first women’s team title with 120 points. No. 3 West Virginia took second with 145. Diljeet Taylor’s Cougars, the Big 12 champions and the No. 1 team in the country, scored 152, good for third. It was a slip of sorts. A year ago they finished second to NC State. Two years ago they won it all. They were chasing a third national championship since 2020, and a seventh in program history. They did not get it. Alabama ended a stretch in which every women’s title since 2020 had belonged to BYU or NC State. NC State’s Hannah Gapes won the individual 6-kilometer race in 18:44.3, breaking her own course record. South Carolina’s Salma Elbadra was second in 18:51.8. BYU’s punch came in a pack, not at the front. Senior Lexi Goff-Thompson led the Cougars in 26th in 19:18.5. Senior Taylor Lovell was 27th in 19:19.5. Senior Riley Chamberlain, in her first and only cross country race of the season, placed 35th in 19:24.3. Sophomore Jane Hedengren, last year’s national runner-up and the Big 12 individual champion, finished 39th in 19:26.1. Senior Taylor Rohatinsky was the fifth scorer in 59th in 19:37.6. Hedengren, among the top runners in the nation, had struggled lately with some health issues and was questionable if she would compete leading into this title race. The top 40 earn All-America honors. That made All-Americans of Goff-Thompson, Lovell, Chamberlain and Hedengren. After questions about whether she would start, Hedengren was about 40th through the first kilometer, according to FloTrack, and finished just inside that line. Then the men. Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto won the 10-kilometer race in 28:27.7, a course record. Alabama’s Dismus Lokira was second in 28:30.8. Oklahoma State’s Denis Kipngetich took third in 28:32.5. No. 1 New Mexico won the team title with 69 points. No. 2 Colorado was second with 107. No. 4 Alabama took the last podium spot with 109. No. 6 BYU was fourth with 195, one point ahead of No. 5 Oregon. Ed Eyestone had almost drawn that map before the gun. In Friday’s Deseret News meet preview, the BYU coach said New Mexico, Colorado and Oklahoma State “will be tough to dethrone.” He added that “the fourth spot” would go to “whichever team comes with their A-game between Oregon, Alabama, Iowa State and us.” Two of those three held. Oklahoma State slipped to seventh with 240 points. Alabama, one of the four he listed for fourth, climbed onto the podium. BYU won the fight he actually forecast, by a single point. “If we can get five All-Americans (top 40 finishes), typically if you score under 200 points, you will be on the podium,” Eyestone said before the race. The Cougars got under 200. They did not get five All-Americans, and they did not get the podium. Tayvon Kitchen led at 3 kilometers and was second at 5 kilometers before finishing 11th in 28:51.0. Isaac Hedengren was 20th in 29:00.4. James Corrigan placed 39th in 29:16.7. All three earned All-America honors. Noah Jenkins, the fourth scorer, was 58th in 29:32.1. Dalton Mortensen, whom Eyestone had named among his top five, finished 114th in 30:12.0. The BYU men have won national titles in 2019 and 2024. This was a hard fourth. Among other Utah schools, No. 15 Utah finished 13th in the women’s race with 374 points. Erin Vringer led the Utes in 43rd in 19:27.5. Utah Valley’s Caren Kipsirat placed 69th in 19:47.0. Utah State’s Natalie Swain was 139th in 20:28.5. Utah Valley’s Sila Kiplagat finished 112th in the men’s race in 30:09.6. Alabama left with a first women’s title and a men’s bronze. New Mexico left with the men’s trophy. BYU left with a women’s podium and a men’s fourth, still chasing the Saturday that ends with a trophy. BYU men's cross country coach Ed Eyestone coaches his team during the UVU Invitational in Orem, Utah, on Sept. 4, 2026. | Emma Thomas, BYU Photo

item.title: Josh Downs Describes How Chiefs Trade Went Down
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs caused a stir ahead of the NFL trade deadline . They made a move to land Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts to address their need at wide receiver. He described how the deal went down. Downs debuted for his new team in Week 10 versus the Atlanta Falcons. He finished with four receptions on five targets for 53 yards and one touchdown, showing that he is already building a strong connection with Patrick Mahomes. The star quarterback completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions. The Colts received a fourth- and fifth-round pick in exchange for the fourth-year wideout. Josh Downs entered the league as the No. 79 overall pick in the third round in 2023. He starred for the North Carolina Tar Heels in college, earning two first-team All-ACC honors. Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) catches a pass during warmup s Sunday, Dec. 28, 2025, ahead of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Josh Downs Discusses His Trade To The Chiefs Josh Downs talked about when he found out he was headed to Kansas City. He highlighted that everything happened fast and how quickly his life changed. My whole life just changed in two-and-a-half hours,” Downs said. “I still got a house in Indy that I need to clear out and stuff. We didn’t really know what was going to happen at all. So it was like 3.30, 3.45-ish. I had texted my team pastor with the Colts and told him, I think I’m going to come to Bible study Wednesday night. I get a text from the Colts higher ups and they’re like, ‘Can you come see me?’ I was like, ‘Dang.’ And then I got a text from Patrick (Mahomes) then. I was like, ‘Oh, dang.’ Me and my dad were outside and I was like, ‘Dad, they just traded me to the Chiefs.’ “It was kind of like a buzzer-beater trade because it was like 3:50 at that time. It was kind of like a buzzer beater-trade because the trade deadline was in 10 minutes. So I had to go turn in all my stuff and then get on a plane like three hours later.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kansas City Chiefs (@chiefs) The move now allows Downs to be part of a legitimate Super Bowl contender with a chance to win the first title of his NFL career. Kansas City is currently 7-2 and at the top of the AFC West. The team entered the season with a chip on its shoulder, looking to prove that they should be one of the championship favorites. item.title: Dak Prescott Loses 3 Offensive Pieces as Cowboys Rule Out 5 Players for Week 11
item.description: Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns against the San Francisco 49ers last Sunday. Despite his stellar outing the Dallas Cowboys surrendered 584 total yards and could not escape a narrow 46-40 defeat. Now the veteran quarterback faces a sudden roster crunch ahead of Sunday’s home game against the Tennessee Titans. Friday’s final injury report revealed that Dallas ruled out five total players, including three key offensive pieces around Prescott. Dak Prescott faces sudden offensive shuffle after Cowboys rule out five players All five sidelined players missed every practice session this week before receiving their final game designations. On offense, Prescott will be without right guard Tyler Booker, tight end Jake Ferguson and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo due to lower-body injuries. Nov 23, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; A general view of a Dallas Cowboys helmet before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Booker and cornerback DaRon Bland both suffered high ankle sprains during the loss to San Francisco. Booker started all 10 games this season and posted an impressive 83 Pro Football Focus grade that ranks fourth among all guards. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed concern after the 49ers loss about losing both starters, saying , “The two big ones I think will be Book with the ankle and Bland with the ankle. Both those guys are going to get X-rays, MRIs, and stuff like that. Both those guys could miss a little bit of time.” Ferguson remains sidelined with knee and ankle sprains suffered against Indianapolis in Week 9. He ranks third on the team with four touchdown catches and will miss his second straight contest. Mingo also sits out with an ankle injury. Cowboys Face Secondary Losses and Offensive Adjustments Against Titans The defensive backfield took an equal hit as Dallas lost Bland and safety P.J. Locke. Bland recorded 38 tackles and seven pass deflections across 10 games this year. Locke remains in concussion protocol after suffering a head injury late in the Nov. 8 win over Indianapolis. The Cowboys also listed safety Jalen Thompson and cornerback Devin Moore alongside tight end Luke Schoonmaker and linebacker Jaishawn Barham as questionable. Offensively, T.J. Bass will step in for Booker at right guard while Prescott continues to depend on top target George Pickens. Pickens recorded 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns against the 49ers. Prescott enters Week 11 with 2,724 passing yards and 21 touchdowns against six interceptions. Even with a shorthanded roster, Dallas opens as an 8.5-point favorite against a Titans unit surrendering a league-worst 266.9 passing yards per game. However, with the Cowboys ranking dead last in total defense at 393.8 yards allowed per contest, Sunday could turn into another high-scoring battle. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Loses Three Offensive Starters as Chiefs Rule Out Key Trio for Week 11
item.description: Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdowns to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to a 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. That convincing win pushed Kansas City to 7-2 and kept them locked in a tight battle atop the AFC West standings. Now the six-time Pro Bowler faces an unexpected challenge ahead of Sunday’s Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Friday’s final injury report revealed that the franchise ruled out three starting offensive players, including two key protectors on his line and his lead running back. Andy Reid confirms Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith and Kenneth Walker III out against Cardinals Pat practiced fully all week despite knee and elbow designations. Tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Rashee Rice were also cleared to play on Sunday. However, right tackle Jaylon Moore, right guard Trey Smith and running back Kenneth Walker III will sit out against Arizona. None of the three starters practiced on Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Oct 7, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; A general view of a Kansas City Chiefs helmet against the New Orleans Saints during the second half at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Addressing their recovery after Friday’s final session, head coach Andy Reid said, “The people that DNP today were Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith, and Kenneth Walker, all of which are improving. Look forward to the challenge of playing Arizona — fast, aggressive team.” Andy Reid’s Friday injury update ahead of Arizona: “The people that DNP today were Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith, and Kenneth Walker, all of which are improving… Look for the challenge of playing Arizona… Fast, aggressive team.” Three OUT. Home test. | Chiefs on YouTube https://t.co/VUSVm7Ke35 — Daily Chiefs (@Daily_Chiefs_) November 20, 2026 Moore hurt his ankle in the third quarter of a Week 9 win over the Jets and will miss his second straight game. Smith left the Falcons matchup in the first half with a concussion and remains in league protocol. Walker also sat out against Atlanta due to a groin injury. Chiefs turn to reshuffled right side and rookie back against Cardinals Replacing the entire right side of the offensive line creates a big challenge for Kansas City. Mike Caliendo is in line to start at right guard for Smith while Joshua Ezeudu steps in at right tackle for Moore. Caliendo has struggled in pass protection this season by allowing 10 total pressures along with three sacks and two quarterback hits. Pro Football Focus ranks him 67th out of 77 qualified guards with a 48.3 overall grade. Ezeudu brings much stronger numbers to the right edge with a 73.9 PFF grade across 171 snaps this year. The Chiefs also signed massive 6-foot-7 veteran tackle Fred Johnson to the practice squad this week for extra insurance. “They’re all going to have a shot to get in there and go,” Reid said of his lineman rotation. “Everybody has a lot of trust in Mike if he’s the one in there playing.” Chiefs HC Andy Reid says Fred Johnson

The fifth-round pick exploded for 171 scrimmage yards against Atlanta by rushing 22 times for 101 yards while catching six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns. item.title: Who is Evans Chuba? What to know about Purdue football starting QB
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − After 22 consecutive starts at quarterback with Ryan Browne , Purdue football went a different direction to begin Saturday's home finale against Wisconsin. Evans Chuba earned his first career start. It marked Chuba's fifth appearance as a Boilermaker . He came into the field late in the first half against Iowa on Nov. 14 on a third-and-1, his first snap in a still competitive game. Prior to Saturday's start, Chuba was 14-for-19 this season, throwing for 142 yards, including a touchdown against Notre Dame. Chuba played the first series against Wisconsin, throwing two incompletions on a three-and-out, before Browne checked in for the second series. More: Purdue-Wisconsin score today: Live updates as Boilers use two quarterbacks Here's what to know about Chuba, who has been Purdue's backup quarterback this season, his second with the Boilermakers . Evans Chuba is from Cananda with an eclectic breakfast palate Chuba grew up in Montreal, Quebec. Growing up, he did not like milk and had an affinity for mixing alternative drink choices with his cereal, he admitted this season during training camp. "With cereal, I put fruit punch, some days I even dabble with some 7Up, Sprite," Chuba said. "So you're eating the cereal and it's popping in your mouth." Chuba started his career elsewhere As a freshman in 2024, Chuba played at Washington State. He never saw the field for the Cougars and transferred to Purdue in the spring. Chuba did not see the field during the 2025 season at Purdue. Before this season, it had been awhile with in game reps Chuba attended Clearwater Academy in Florida, but missed his senior season with an injury. His first college playing time came in the 2026 season opener against Indiana State, when Chuba completed 4 of 5 passes for 29 yards. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. This article originally appeared on Lafayette Journal & Courier: Who is Evans Chuba? What to know about Purdue football starting QB

item.title: Thomason's heart typifies Wrexham - Parkinson
item.description: George Thomason has scored twice in his past three Wrexham appearances [John Mallett/ProSports/Shutterstock] Phil Parkinson says George Thomason possesses the key qualities Wrexham need in their squad following the midfielder's match-winner at Lincoln City. The 25-year-old robbed Daniel Oyegoke of possession before coolly slotting beyond George Wickens in the 82nd minute to earn the visitors a 1-0 victory over the Imps at ProAmpac Stadium. "He just typifies what we want here at Wrexham in terms of his heart, and he's a good player," Parkinson told BBC Radio Wales. Thomason started the contest at left wing-back but shifted to his preferred central midfield role after Ollie Rathbone was withdrawn through injury. And following his vital moment of quality late on, Parkinson praised Thomason for once again demonstrating his ability to operate in different roles. "Some of his link-up play was really good. Rathbone gets a dead leg, and we move him [Thomason] infield," Parkinson added. "He came to us as a midfield player; we converted him last year and he was probably close to getting player of the year in that position. "We need versatility and he showed that today." Thomason strike earns Wrexham victory at Lincoln EFL warns clubs over social media posts The win over Lincoln means Wrexham - who remain 14th in the Championship table - have claimed seven of the previous nine points on offer. They claimed victory without attacking talents Callum O'Hare, Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Sam Smith, who are all sidelined with injuries. However, the injury sustained by Rathbone at Lincoln does not appear to be serious, Parkinson went on to confirm. "It's just a dead leg. He tried to stay on; at first I thought it was his ankle, which worried me," the manager said of the 30-year-old midfielder. "It was a bang to his thigh. With the quality of Jacques [Ekomie] to come on and with Thommo to move infield, we had no need to risk him." Having withdrawn from Wales' squad to face Norway and Portugal in the Nations League due to injury, Kieffer Moore played the full match against Lincoln. But Parkinson was confident the 34-year-old would be available to feature against the Imps given the work the striker undertook during the international break. "It was more a problem with his back. We would never have risked him, but he had a full week in the international break of gym work and strengthening work," Parkinson said. "We've felt him into training gradually this week. "I think in games like that with his height in the middle of the goal, it's so important. "I was tempted to bring him off, and we wanted to try and win it with Cadz [Bailey Cadamarteri] at the top end of the pitch, but Kieffer's a colossus in defensive situations as well." item.title: Newcastle United v Arsenal: Premier League – live
item.description: ⚽️ Premier League updates from the 5.30pm GMT kick-off ⚽️ Live scores | Latest table | Follow us on TikTok | Mail Rob “There is an ebb and a flow to Arsenal’s front three, isn’t there?” writes Charles Antaki. “Eze, Havertz, Madueke – in any given game, one will delight and the other two disappoint; one will score and the other two will be all over the place; one will bring joy, and the other two will invite cursing and the gnashing of teeth. And all this is not to mention the chap lurking on the bench. Personally – I admit it – I’d rather have three fully functioning goal machines, but there we are.” We hate it when our teams become successful. He’s prepared emotionally; he knows to accept. We have to be very dominant emotionally to attack Newcastle in the way we want, and he’s ready to do that. Continue reading...

item.title: Dabo Swinney Hears Loud ‘Dabo’ Chants as Clemson Players Hold Up Viral Sign Amid Mounting Criticism
item.description: Dabo Swinney faced criticism over his roster philosophy and his future with the program after the Clemson Tigers suffered a 20-6 loss to a struggling Georgia Tech squad on November 14. His players answered the noise in style during their very next game in Durham on his 57th birthday. The Tigers stunned the No. 24 Duke Blue Devils as double-digit underdogs on Friday. Following the convincing 20-10 win, players gathered on the sideline for a heartfelt celebration to silence critics who claimed Swinney had lost his locker room. Clemson stars back Dabo Swinney on his birthday after turbulent week Offensive linemen Harris Sewell and Grant Wise led teammates toward the stands after the game. In a clip shared by FOX Carolina reporter Caroline Soro, they could be seen holding a fan-made poster reading “Support Swinney” high for the cameras. Louisville football coach Jeff Brohm and Clemson Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney talk before the game against Clemson at L&N Stadium Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. Eventually, fans in the stands also joined the roster by chanting “Dabo” and singing “Happy Birthday” to their longtime coach. Swinney later admitted he spotted the supporter holding that sign and deeply appreciated the gesture. NEW: Clemson players hold up a “Support Swinney” sign as fans chant “Dabo” following the win over Duke. (via @caroline_soro) https://t.co/jCNPCSgJtQ — On3 (@On3) November 21, 2026 Players made that public display after watching their coach take fire from national pundits all week. During his Tuesday press conference, Swinney defended his 18-year tenure and said, “So by 2031, we’re going to win another one. That’s all I can tell you. That’s just what I believe.” Following his remark, ESPN host Tony Kornheiser called the title promise “insanity and delusional” on Pardon the Interruption. Analysts also argued Swinney has failed to adapt to the modern transfer portal and NIL era. He holds a contract through 2031 with a $57 million buyout that left many questioning the direction of the program. The Tigers answered by pulling off the upset despite entering the night with a depleted quarterback room. Starter Tait Reynolds and backup Christopher Vizzina both suffered injuries against Georgia Tech. That forced third-stringer Trent Pearman into his first career start alongside converted wideout Chris Denson. The duo powered a 220-yard rushing attack with a touchdown each while the defense suffocated Duke for just 247 total yards. Swinney pushed back hard against the outside chatter following Friday’s victory, saying , “All this (has) done is galvanize our team. I don’t do this for applause. I’ve had plenty of that. My life is built on the foundation of Christ, but it’s disheartening because I do my best every day. I do my best… Nobody else. Nobody else stands up for Coach Swinney, except them players, except them freaking players that know.” The triumph improves Clemson to 7-4 overall and 5-3 in ACC play. item.title: Royce Lewis to the Dodgers
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 27: Royce Lewis #23 of the Minnesota Twins celebrates as he rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run in the eighth inning during the game between the Texas Rangers and the Minnesota Twins at Target Field on Sunday, September 27, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Andrew Ritter/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for pitcher Bobby Miller and minor league catcher Francisco Espinoza in a trade that was reported Friday. This is an interesting deal to me, in that each team is moving on from a former first round pick and top prospect who has struggled both to stay healthy and to be productive in their time in the majors. Royce Lewis was the #1 overall pick in the 2017 draft out of San Juan Capistrano, California, while Miller was the 29th overall pick in the 2020 draft out of the University of Louisville, after having been picked in the 38th round of the 2017 draft by the Orioles and going unsigned. Miller moved quickly through the minors, making it to AA in 2021 and splitting the 2022 season between AA and AAA. Heading into 2023, Miller was a consensus top 25 prospect in baseball. Ongoing shoulder issues have plagued Miller since then, however, and after putting up a 3.76 ERA in 22 starts for the Dodgers in 2023, he’s split his time between AAA, the majors, and the injured list the past three seasons. Miller threw only 24 innings between AAA and the majors in 2026 due to a shoulder injury that kept him out until late in the season. Lewis was a consensus top 10 prospect in baseball after an impressive first full season as a professional split between low-A and high-A, though offensive struggles after that saw him slip a little bit in the prospect rankings before a torn ACL sidelined him for the entirety of the 2021 season, meaning he saw no official game action for two straight seasons, as the 2020 minor league season was eliminated due to the pandemic. He re-tore his ACL in 2022, costing him most of the season, and played in just 58 major league games in 2023 due to injuries, though his .309/.372/.548 slash line as a shortstop fueled the belief he was a star in the making if he could stay healthy. Unfortunately, while Lewis’s games played per season increased each year thereafter, he still missed significant time due to injury, while his offensive performance slid. The past two seasons, Lewis has slashed .231/.285/.384 in 231 games while manning the corner infield spots. It isn’t immediately clear where the Dodgers will look to play Lewis, given they currently have Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy in the corner infield spots, and Shohei Ohtani is the team’s DH. I’m guessing Lewis goes into a utility role of some sort, with the Dodgers presumably finding ways to get him into the lineup more often if they can get his bat back to where it was earlier in his career. item.content:encoded: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 27: Royce Lewis #23 of the Minnesota Twins celebrates as he rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run in the eighth inning during the game between the Texas Rangers and the Minnesota Twins at Target Field on Sunday, September 27, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Andrew Ritter/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for pitcher Bobby Miller and minor league catcher Francisco Espinoza in a trade that was reported Friday. This is an interesting deal to me, in that each team is moving on from a former first round pick and top prospect who has struggled both to stay healthy and to be productive in their time in the majors. Royce Lewis was the #1 overall pick in the 2017 draft out of San Juan Capistrano, California, while Miller was the 29th overall pick in the 2020 draft out of the University of Louisville, after having been picked in the 38th round of the 2017 draft by the Orioles and going unsigned. Miller moved quickly through the minors, making it to AA in 2021 and splitting the 2022 season between AA and AAA. Heading into 2023, Miller was a consensus top 25 prospect in baseball. Ongoing shoulder issues have plagued Miller since then, however, and after putting up a 3.76 ERA in 22 starts for the Dodgers in 2023, he’s split his time between AAA, the majors, and the injured list the past three seasons. Miller threw only 24 innings between AAA and the majors in 2026 due to a shoulder injury that kept him out until late in the season. Lewis was a consensus top 10 prospect in baseball after an impressive first full season as a professional split between low-A and high-A, though offensive struggles after that saw him slip a little bit in the prospect rankings before a torn ACL sidelined him for the entirety of the 2021 season, meaning he saw no official game action for two straight seasons, as the 2020 minor league season was eliminated due to the pandemic. He re-tore his ACL in 2022, costing him most of the season, and played in just 58 major league games in 2023 due to injuries, though his .309/.372/.548 slash line as a shortstop fueled the belief he was a star in the making if he could stay healthy. Unfortunately, while Lewis’s games played per season increased each year thereafter, he still missed significant time due to injury, while his offensive performance slid. The past two seasons, Lewis has slashed .231/.285/.384 in 231 games while manning the corner infield spots. It isn’t immediately clear where the Dodgers will look to play Lewis, given they currently have Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy in the corner infield spots, and Shohei Ohtani is the team’s DH. I’m guessing Lewis goes into a utility role of some sort, with the Dodgers presumably finding ways to get him into the lineup more often if they can get his bat back to where it was earlier in his career. The Twins, meanwhile, will try to keep Miller healthy, and see where best he fits. Seeing Lewis dealt prompted me to go back and look at the 2017 draft, and I think it is fair to say that the top of the first round has been a disappointment. Here’s how it shakes out: #1 — Royce Lewis, 4.9 bWAR. Unable to stay healthy, stopped hitting, traded. #2 — Hunter Greene, 12.8 bWAR. Looked for a couple of seasons like a legitimate top of the rotation guy, but missed most of 2026 with elbow issues, and then had Tommy John surgery in August. #3 — MacKenzie Gore, 7.2 bWAR. Tantalizing stuff, inability to actualize it, traded twice. #4 — Brendan McKay, -0.1 bWAR. Supposed two-way player became solely a pitcher. Underwent Thoracic Outlet Syndrome surgery, then Tommy John surgery, then suffered a flexor tendon strain and torn UCL while on a rehab assignment after TJS. Now out of baseball. #5 — Kyle Wright, 2.6 bWAR. Stud Vandy pitcher made it to the majors a year after being drafted, bounced between AAA and the majors the next three years, had a breakout 21 win season in 2022, threw just 45 innings between the majors and minors in 2023, and has thrown just 23 innings — all in the minors in 2025 — since due to injuries. Released by the Cubs this past summer without pitching for them in actual game action. #6 — Austin Beck, N/A. Toolsy high school outfielder drafted by the A’s who didn’t hit, missed all of 2023 due to a torn ACL, and retired late in 2024 after 66 games at AA for the Dodgers. #7 — Pavin Smith, 0.3 bWAR. First of two consecutive hitters taken from the University of Virginia. Spent parts of seven seasons with the D-Backs, mostly in a bench role. Currently a free agent. #8 — Adam Haseley, 1.5 bWAR. Second of two consecutive hitters taken from the University of Virginia. Put up 1.8 bWAR as a rookie for the Phillies in 2019 in 67 games, driven largely by his defense. Played just 91 major league games thereafter, largely due to an inability to hit. Traded to the White Sox prior to the 2022 season, non-tendered after the 2023 season, hasn’t signed with anyone since and is presumably out of baseball. #9 — Keston Huerta, 0.9 bWAR. Like Haseley, put up impressive numbers in a partial season in 2019 as a rookie, though in his case it was offense-driven, slashing .303/.368/.570 in 84 games for the Brewers. Has a .203/.389/.381 slash line in 218 games with a -1.0 bWAR since. Spent 2026 playing for Kiwoom in Korea. #10 — Jo Adell, 1.3 bWAR. Underwhelming for the Angels from 2020-26, traded to the Guardians at the deadline in 2026 and slashed .244/.324/.417. After that you had a nice run from #11-13 with Jake Burger, Shane Baz and Trevor Rogers. David Peterson, Tanner Houck and Brent Rooker highlight the rest of the first round, unless you count Drew Rasmussen, who was picked at #31 by the Rays but didn’t sign with them, presumably due to an elbow injury that necessitated Tommy John surgery a few months later. The Brewers ended up signing Rasmussen after taking him in the sixth round in 2018. Rasmussen’s career 15.7 bWAR is the highest of anyone taken in the first round in 2017. The 2017 draft doesn’t get much better after the first round, incidentally. Daulton Varsho and Griffin Canning are the only players selected in the second round to amass at least 2.0 career bWAR this far. Taylor Walls, Connor Wong, Nick Allen, Keegan Thompson and Riley Adams are the 2+ bWAR guys from the third round, though Wong’s 4.2 bWAR is the second highest of the group. Ernie Clement is the only fourth rounder with a positive bWAR, and only three fourth round picks appeared in at least 30 games. Only one fifth round pick from 2017 has a positive bWAR. You may have heard of him. He was the Rangers’ closer this year.

item.title: 'Duty of care': Players' union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
item.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala (L) speaks to coach Vincent Kompany (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Global players' union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers' union said recent public comments made by Bayern's honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a "coordinated campaign" to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations". "A club of Bayern's standing should know better," the international union for professional football players said. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala... Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern's top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a "neurological disorder" which can lead to "temporary but treatable seizures". Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. "Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium," Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. "If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency -- because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable." Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. dwi/ea

In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers' union said recent public comments made by Bayern's honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a "coordinated campaign" to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations". "A club of Bayern's standing should know better," the international union for professional football players said. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala... Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." item.title: Martin O'Neill's post-match reaction on CelticPlayer
item.description: Martin O'Neill's post-match reaction on CelticPlayer It may have been a frosty day in Glasgow’s East End today (Saturday, November 21) but Celtic turned the heat up on St Mirren , rushing to a three-goal lead by half time and adding a fourth early in the second half. The visitors pulled a goal back from the penalty spot but it wasn’t enough to halt the Hoops’ procession to another three points which, for the time being, puts them seven points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership table. Speaking to CelticPlayer after the match, Martin O’Neill gave his assessment on a good day’s work from the Bhoys. “I’m delighted.” The Manager said. “We played some really good stuff, particularly in the first half. “We had a really good lead at half time, we made a few substitutions during the second half, but overall I’m delighted with the performance and team. “It was a matter of being on the front foot early on in the game. Don’t be passive, be strong, be aggressive and I think we did all of that.” Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain opened the scoring with a finish following some good play from Yang, whilst Luke McCowan rounded off the first-half goals with a fine finish of his own. Martin O’Neill was keen to praise both men in his post-match reflections, telling CelticPlayer: “I’m really pleased for both of them. Absolutely delighted. “Alex has waited for his chance, and he’s a very fine player, a really terrific passer as well too. He took the goal magnificently. “Luke took his goal great, very well indeed. And I’m just pleased for the whole team, but particularly pleased for those lads.” Fixtures Celtic Vs. St. Mirren - Sat, Nov 21st 2026, 15:00

item.title: Serie A Side Interested In Nottingham Forest Winger
item.description: Serie A Side Interested In Nottingham Forest Winger Callum Hudson-Odoi to Roma? Nottingham Forest Face January Transfer Decision Amid £10m Interest Nottingham Forest could have a January decision to make over Callum Hudson-Odoi, with TeamTalk reporting that Roma have identified the winger as a possible attacking addition. Sources cited in the report state that Roma are weighing up a move for the 26-year-old as they search for greater depth and quality in wide areas. The Serie A club are said to see Hudson-Odoi as one of a number of options, with the report explaining that he is “viewed as an alternative or secondary target behind Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens”, while “a loan with an option for summer is a doable deal”. Roma interest grows around Hudson-Odoi The background to that interest is clear enough. Hudson-Odoi “has found opportunities limited under Forest manager Oliver Glasner this season”, and the numbers outlined in the report underline that point. He “has made only five appearances for Forest this season, all from the bench, and has played only 45 minutes in the Premier League for the Tricky Trees”. For a player who has previously offered goals, assists and attacking thrust, that is a notable drop in involvement. Roma’s need is also specific. They are “seeking a left-sided attacking option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini” and appear to believe Hudson-Odoi could suit that requirement if circumstances align. Nottingham Forest stance on £10m deal Forest, however, are not under immediate pressure. Hudson-Odoi signed a new contract in August 2025, extending his stay until 2028, which leaves the club in a strong negotiating position. That matters in any talks, especially when one source quoted in the report has “suggested a figure around £10million could appeal to Forest”. Photo: IMAGO Even then, the picture is far from advanced. “No formal contact between clubs has yet been made,” and Forest are described as holding firm because of both contract length and squad depth value. The report adds that the club “may prefer a temporary deal that retains a future sale option with a better value rather than a permanent exit in January”. January transfer window could hinge on player choice There is a practical balance to strike. On one hand, “the player’s reduced role makes a January departure more likely”. On the other, Forest “are shrewd negotiators and will want to recoup a decent fee”. That combination often slows early interest before the market sharpens. For now, the situation remains open. “Whether Roma’s interest develops into a formal approach will depend on Forest’s willingness to negotiate and the winger’s willingness to move mod season.” If that changes, Forest may soon have to decide whether retaining useful depth is worth more than a profitable sale. Our View There is no rush to cash in here unless the deal suits Forest properly. A £10million figure sounds respectable when set against the fee paid to sign Hudson-Odoi, but context matters more

Sources cited in the report state that Roma are weighing up a move for the 26-year-old as they search for greater depth and quality in wide areas. The Serie A club are said to see Hudson-Odoi as one of a number of options, with the report explaining that he is “viewed as an alternative or secondary target behind Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens”, while “a loan with an option for summer is a doable deal”. Roma interest grows around Hudson-Odoi The background to that interest is clear enough. Hudson-Odoi “has found opportunities limited under Forest manager Oliver Glasner this season”, and the numbers outlined in the report underline that point. He “has made only five appearances for Forest this season, all from the bench, and has played only 45 minutes in the Premier League for the Tricky Trees”. For a player who has previously offered goals, assists and attacking thrust, that is a notable drop in involvement. Roma’s need is also specific. They are “seeking a left-sided attacking option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini” and appear to believe Hudson-Odoi could suit that requirement if circumstances align. Nottingham Forest stance on £10m deal Forest, however, are not under immediate pressure. Hudson-Odoi signed a new contract in August 2025, extending his stay until 2028, which leaves the club in a strong negotiating position. That matters in any talks, especially when one source quoted in the report has “suggested a figure around £10million could appeal to Forest”. Photo: IMAGO Even then, the picture is far from advanced. “No formal contact between clubs has yet been made,” and Forest are described as holding firm because of both contract length and squad depth value. The report adds that the club “may prefer a temporary deal that retains a future sale option with a better value rather than a permanent exit in January”. January transfer window could hinge on player choice There is a practical balance to strike. On one hand, “the player’s reduced role makes a January departure more likely”. On the other, Forest “are shrewd negotiators and will want to recoup a decent fee”. That combination often slows early interest before the market sharpens. For now, the situation remains open. “Whether Roma’s interest develops into a formal approach will depend on Forest’s willingness to negotiate and the winger’s willingness to move mod season.” If that changes, Forest may soon have to decide whether retaining useful depth is worth more than a profitable sale. Our View There is no rush to cash in here unless the deal suits Forest properly. A £10million figure sounds respectable when set against the fee paid to sign Hudson-Odoi, but context matters more than optics. He still has quality, he still has a contract until 2028, and he still offers something different in the squad when used well. The frustrating part is that this feels like a player who could still contribute far more than his minutes suggest. If he has slipped down the pecking order, that naturally opens the door to interest, but letting him go on the cheap in January would feel premature. Forest have built a reputation for being smart in the market and this is exactly the sort of situation where patience should bring leverage. A loan with a summer option makes more sense than an immediate permanent exit, especially if Roma are testing the waters rather than committing fully. If they really want him, they can pay for the privilege. If not, Forest keep a talented attacking option for the second half of the season. There is also the squad dynamic to consider. Depth across the front line matters, injuries happen quickly, and a player who has already shown he can deliver in previous campaigns should not be ushered out too easily. Unless Hudson-Odoi pushes strongly to leave, the sensible play is to hold firm, protect the asset and make sure any agreement reflects both his ability and Forest’s position of strength.

item.title: Giannis And Heat Show Growth, But Roster Gaps Remain
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat have found their rhythm after a shaky start. They have won 9 of their last 11 games to sit at 9-6 on the season. This surge includes a six-game winning streak that has fans feeling hopeful again. Yet, the team still faces a hard test to prove they belong among the elite. Giannis Antetokounmpo sees the same reality as the coaching staff. He notes that the team is neither terrible nor perfect right now. Antetokounmpo has been clear about the team’s current spot in the league. He told reporters that the Heat are not as bad as people say they are, but they are also not as good as people say they are. This middle ground is where the team must stay focused. The Greek star emphasized that keeping a steady mindset is key to survival. He urged his teammates to keep their heads down and build good habits daily. The Heat have a long road ahead with 67 games remaining. Giannis Changes How the Offense Works Giannis Antetokounmpo is scoring points and reshaping the entire offense. Coach Erik Spoelstra says the star forward is helping the team’s attack grow exponentially. The system works because Giannis moves without the ball and involves his teammates. He makes simple decisions based on the defense he faces. He told reporters, according to Sun Sentinel , “If I have one guy in front of me, I tend to go. If I have two or three guys in front of me, I pass.” This approach has pushed the Heat to rank second in offensive rating over their last 11 games. Davion Mitchell has thrived alongside this new style of play. Mitchell currently leads the NBA with 9.0 assists per game. He praised Giannis for trusting teammates and getting them into a rhythm. Mitchell noted that the offense feels like night and day compared to the start of the season. The Heat have used a unique rotation where Giannis starts but also plays with reserves. This allows Bam Adebayo to shine as a featured scorer while still working with Giannis. The Backup Point Guard Problem Despite the wins, a major hole exists at the backup point guard spot. Davion Mitchell has played heavy minutes, ranking among the league leaders in fourth-quarter action. The team lacks a true Plan B if Mitchell gets hurt or rests. Dru Smith is the closest option, but he has seen only 56 minutes of action this year. Other players like Ryan Conwell and Pelle Larsson have stepped up at times. However, the lack of depth remains a worry for the front office. Bleacher Report recently gave the Heat a “C+” for their first month of play. This grade reflects a rough start where the team began 0-4 before finding their stride. The report noted that while the guard play has improved, the team still has work to do. The Heat have historically thrived as underdogs, and that role might fuel them further. Critics were right about the early struggles, but the team has responded with a strong run. The Heat have historically thrived as underdogs, and that role might fuel them further. Critics were right about the early struggles, but the team has responded with a strong run. Next Test Against a Tough Schedule The Heat will face a brutal stretch of games to test their consistency. After a three-day break, the team plays the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night at Kaseya Center. The Sunday night game at Kaseya Center closes out a five-game homestand that has opened 4-0. Following that, the Heat must travel to face the Philadelphia 76ers, New York Knicks, and Cleveland Cavaliers. These road games will be much harder than recent wins against weaker opponents. The team recently defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, a former home for Giannis. The victory improved the Heat to 9-6 while dropping the Bucks to a 1-15 record. Giannis scored 27 points in that win but skipped the post-game handshake line. He explained that he tries to lock in as much as he can when he plays basketball. Reporters were told by him that the situation seemed normal and not strange. The Heat will face the Bucks again in Milwaukee on January 28, 2027.

item.title: 'We know what the history of this game is like' - Ethan Ampadu hails Leeds performance at Chelsea after ending 27-year wait for away win
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-CHELSEA-LEEDS - AFP Leeds United captain Ethan Ampadu has praised his side's clinical display after the Whites secured a commanding 4-1 victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, their first away win against the Blues in more than a quarter of a century. The historic result has thrust the Yorkshire giants into the European conversation following a dominant second-half performance in west London. A historic afternoon in west London The weight of history finally lifted off Leeds United's shoulders on Saturday as they recorded their first league victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999. In a fixture defined by a fierce, long-standing rivalry, the visitors showed remarkable resilience to come from behind and secure a result that will live long in the memory of the travelling supporters. Speaking shortly after the final whistle, the Welsh international highlighted the importance of meeting the high expectations set by the fanbase. Ampadu told reporters: 'We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance.' Despite the celebratory mood, the 26-year-old midfielder was quick to point out that the team must use this result as a platform for further growth rather than a final destination. Addressing the tactical evolution of the squad under the current regime, Ampadu added: 'People talk about turning points and we have to learn about stuff that didn't work and try to better that.' Okafor shines as Chelsea crumble The match did not initially go to plan for the visitors, as Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha . The Dutch forward, making his full debut for the London club following a summer move, opened his account in the 25th minute with a powerful left-footed strike. However, the lead lasted only three minutes before Noah Okafor capitalised on defensive chaos within the Blues' backline to slide an equaliser into the far corner, shifting the momentum back towards the Whites. Leeds eventually took the lead from the penalty spot after referee Michael Oliver penalised Morgan Rogers for using his arm to block a goal-bound effort from Jayden Bogle, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin confidently sending the spot-kick into the bottom corner. The visitors tightened their grip on the game in the 58th minute when Okafor reacted to a bouncing ball by hooking it into the roof of the net. Brenden Aaronson then put the result beyond doubt deep into stoppage time, racing clear from the halfway line before calmly slotting the ball into the bottom corner. European ambitions and reality checks The three points have lifted Leeds United to sixth in the Premier League standings, leaving them just a single point behind fourth-placed Bournemouth in the hunt for Champions League football. Reflecting on the talk of a European charge, the captain noted: 'We have to be realistic and understand how hard this league is. We need to back this up next week, if we don'

item.title: Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma
item.description: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala sits on the bench prior to the start of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich are not ruling out the sale of Jamal Musiala as fresh statements from supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have escalated the situation surrounding the midfielder. Musiala has been struggling with fitness since a serious injury at last year's Club World Cup, which forced him to miss half of the 2025-26 season. He made his comeback from yet another injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday evening. However, there are concerns over his health after he collapsed earlier this year during two pre-season games. He later went public about a neurological condition. "He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal," Rummenigge said after the draw with Cologne. He said that selling the player "it's not out of the question. We suspect it will be difficult for him to get back to his previous level." However, Rummenigge added that he can't imagine another club would buy Musiala "under these circumstances. We have to think about the financial implications." According to the Bild newspaper, Musiala's medication remains a major challenge. Whenever the illness is fully suppressed, side effects are said to occur repeatedly, preventing the player from consistently reaching his maximum performance level. The report added that attempts to manage these side effects through alternative medication cannot rule out the possibility of further absence seizures. Bayern not aware of condition at contract extension In February 2025, Musiala signed a new contract with Bayern until June 2030. However, according to club president Herbert Hainer, the German giants were not aware of his neurological condition. "I didn't know about it, and I don't think anyone at the club knew either. I also don't know whether he himself was aware of it. I certainly don't believe that was the case," Hainer told reporters after Bayern's annual general meeting on Saturday. He insisted that Musiala's health is the top priority and that "everyone involved wants Jamal to return to the level he was at." "And we are doing everything we can to make that happen. We are giving him every possible support and all the time he needs. Of course, we all have concerns and thoughts about the club. That is also part of our responsibility. But Jamal's health comes first, above all else," he told reporters after Bayern's annual general meeting on Saturday. However, there are concerns over his health after he collapsed earlier this year during two pre-season games. He later went public about a neurological condition. "He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal," Rummenigge said after the draw with Cologne. He said that selling the player "it's not out of the question. We suspect it will be difficult for him to get back to his previous level." However, Rummenigge added that he can't imagine another club would buy Musiala "under these circumstances. We have to think about the financial implications." According to the Bild newspaper, Musiala's medication remains a major challenge. Whenever the illness is fully suppressed, side effects are said to occur repeatedly, preventing the player from consistently reaching his maximum performance level. The report added that attempts to manage these side effects through alternative medication cannot rule out the possibility of further absence seizures. Bayern not aware of condition at contract extension In February 2025, Musiala signed a new contract with Bayern until June 2030. However, according to club president Herbert Hainer, the German giants were not aware of his neurological condition. "I didn't know about it, and I don't think anyone at the club knew either. I also don't know whether he himself was aware of it. I certainly don't believe that was the case," Hainer told reporters after Bayern's annual general meeting on Saturday. He insisted that Musiala's health is the top priority and that "everyone involved wants Jamal to return to the level he was at." "And we are doing everything we can to make that happen. We are giving him every possible support and all the time he needs. Of course, we all have concerns and thoughts about the club. That is also part of our responsibility. But Jamal's health comes first, above all else," he told reporters after Bayern's annual general meeting on Saturday. Asked whether it was helpful that members of the supervisory board and the executive board publicly put that kind of pressure on a 23-year-old player, Hainer said that there is no pressure, but "I think the statements made by all those involved were quite clear." Fan criticizes public comments During the AGM, a Bayern fan, who presented himself as a neurologist, criticized the way the club is handling Musiala's situation in public. "I have enormous respect for Jamal Musiala for speaking about his situation publicly. I know how incredibly difficult that can be for people going through something like this. And in a situation like this, what you need is support," Jonatan Hoffmann said. "Support of the kind expressed by people like Max Eberl and Vincent Kompany, who have stood by him and had his back. What I don't believe is helpful in a situation like this is publicly calling him out and questioning whether he will ever reach his previous level again, as Mr Dreesen (sporting director Jan-Christian Dreesen) and Mr Hoeness (honorary president Uli Hoeness) have done, and, above all, as Mr Rummenigge took to an extreme yesterday." "In my view, that has very little to do with the FC Bayern family. And, dear Jamal, if you happen to see or hear this in any way: I believe in you. Many people believe in you. Show them what you can do. Come back stronger!" Hoeness recently has also expressed doubts whether Musiala would ever return to his previous level of play. "He has an illness that is not easily curable, but can be controlled to some extent with medication. But whether he will ever again have the performance level he once had..." "But now he is still getting paid. Just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: what he can now deliver is no longer what was in the contract," he said referring to Musiala's deal until 2030.

item.title: Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments
item.description: Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy [Getty Images] Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better". Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction". Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had" . The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested the deal may need to be renegotiated. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better." Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala? Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September. He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months". item.title: Three Victory to Keys: LSU vs. Tennessee
item.description: The LSU Tigers will look to end their losing skid in a tough environment today as they travel to Knoxville to take on #9 Tennessee. Here’s what the Purple and Gold have to accomplish if they want to win on the road today: Run The Ball: LSU has found success in the ground game in recent weeks, including a 45-yard touchdown run from Dilin Jones. However, the offensive playcalling has not allowed them to find a rhythm in the run game. Call the plays, run the ball, and don’t get discouraged if you only get a yard or two early on. Keep Playing Strong Defense : This season, the Tigers have played like a top 10 defense, and that was evident through most of the last two games where they held Alabama to 150 yards and 10 points through three quarters and then held Arch Manning and Texas to just 10 points before collapsing in the fourth. Keep your foot on the gas defensively, pressure whoever is at QB for the Vols, and don’t let it fall apart in the fourth. Don’t Overthink It : Lane Kiffin has been known throughout his career as an overthinker, and it’s come up in massive ways during this losing streak. Play calling has gotten conservative, and it has almost felt like this team was playing not to lose, and it cost you two critical games. Even if you get out to a lead, continue doing what’s worked for you, take care of the football, and take the victory. The LSU Tigers and Tennessee Volunteers are set to do battle in Neyland Stadium in Knoxville at 2:30 p.m. CT on ABC.

item.title: The Lewis Moody message that inspired England to record win over New Zealand
item.description: England captain Maro Itoje revealed an inspirational speech from predecessor Lewis Moody inspired his side to a record win over New Zealand at Twickenham. Moody, a 2003 World Cup winner who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, joined Itoje and his side to stare down the All Blacks ’ haka in an emotional pre-match answer to the traditional Maori challenge. The 48-year-old had presented Steve Borthwick ’s squad with their match shirts on Friday evening and addressed the side, setting the tone for a 37-12 success – their largest over the All Blacks. “I got a call from [England’s Rugby Football Union chief executive] Bill Sweeney a couple of weeks ago and he got a message from Lewis' team about how we could potentially support Lewis on this game day,” Itoje explained. “Then the idea was floated about him potentially joining us for the haka and I took it away. I spoke to a lot of the senior guys in the team and there was overwhelming support to support Lewis. Lewis Moody joined England for a spell-binding pre-match display (Getty) “Lewis is such an inspirational man. He was an inspirational player and given his diagnosis the players jumped at the opportunity to support him. I think he and his family gave us that extra lift today. “”He came to spend some time with us yesterday. He presented us our shirt for today's game. He spoke to us, addressed us. There's no doubt that his presence, him joining us for the haka, him spending time with us gave us an extra lift. He was one of the guys I looked up to as a young boy playing rugby. I have the honour and privilege of captaining this great team, and to be able to welcome him onto the field is a memory that will live with me for the rest of my life. As an England group, we are so proud to be able to support him.” Moody was a try-scorer against New Zealand in 2002, the first of back-to-back victories over the All Blacks from a side that went on to win the World Cup. Itoje’s team have now emulated that first achievement having also beaten their opposition last November. The two teams could yet meet again on Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham. “The great thing about sport and the great thing about rugby is that it keeps presenting you with opportunities,” Itoje said. “We've had a good result today. We're very proud of our performance today but the great thing is that next week there's a new opportunity in front of us. “Whatever happens, we don't know exactly what's going to happen but whoever we play, whatever the circumstance, there's a new opportunity ahead of us and I guess we have the chance, we have the opportunity to take it.”

item.title: European football: Noslin’s double helps Lazio beat Lecce and extend Serie A lead
item.description: Dortmund beat Mönchengladbach in Bundesliga Harry Kane vows to return after Bayern injury Lazio continued to underline their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 ⁠home win against Lecce as Gennaro Gattuso’s side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead ⁠at the top ⁠of the ​standings. Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style with a 90th-minute ⁠strike as Lazio earned their 10th victory in 12 games to move to 32 points, four ahead of Inter Milan ⁠who travel to Atlanta on Sunday. Como are fourth on 26 points after ​a 2-0 win over Cagliari ‌thanks to goals from ‌Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha. Continue reading...

item.title: Walker Kessler flashes ‘f–k yeah’ moment in game of ‘f–k nos’
item.description: As Walker Kessler walked into the interview room, he uttered four words. “A win’s a win.” The Lakers, who have the NBA’s best record at 14-3, had eked past the Kings (1-14), who are in the league’s cellar. Walker Kessler (14) of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images For Kessler, the Lakers’ 106-104 win on Friday was mostly forgettable. He got lit into by Lakers coach JJ Redick at halftime after only having six points and one rebound before turning things around to finish with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocked shots. He missed two free throws with 5.3 seconds left and the Lakers up, 106-104, a blemish that would’ve been much worse had Zach LaVine not missed his go-ahead 3-point attempt with 0.9 seconds left. But let’s focus on the positive. In a few days, no one is going to remember that the Lakers trailed the Kings by as much as 11 points in a game with 10 lead changes and 15 ties. All that anyone is going to remember is the W. Oh, and there was a major highlight. Kessler has already proven himself as an excellent rim defender and rebounder , but on Friday he revealed that there are some more tricks in his bag. With 11:42 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Lakers trailing the Kings, 84-82, Collin Sexton passed the ball to the 7-foot-1 center in the corner. Kessler then fired a 24-foot jumper which swished through the net. It was his first 3-pointer this season. So, you know, he’s shooting a stunning 100% from beyond the arc. Dylan Cardwell of the Sacramento Kings plays defense on Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It wasn’t exactly the play Redick called. He said it was “unorganized,” adding, “I’m not sure why [Kessler] was even in the corner.” But Redick loved it. “I didn’t bat an eye when he shot it,” Redick said. Redick then revealed why he was unfazed. During the preseason, after Redick drew an ATO that involved Kessler, the center wanted to make sure he did his due diligence by inquiring about all possible scenarios. Walker Kessler grabs a rebound during the NBA Cup game at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “We break the huddle and he’s like, ‘Coach, what do you want me to do if the ball finds me and we don’t get a layup on this play?’ Redick recalled Kessler asking. “And I said, ‘Shoot it.’ And he goes, ‘F–k yeah.'” So in a game with so many “F–k nos,” Kessler finally got his moment. “I feel good,” Kessler said, adding a caveat. “Should’ve made those free throws.”

item.title: Emegha And Lavia Get 7 | Chelsea Players Rated In Disappointing Loss Vs Leeds United
item.description: Emegha And Lavia Get 7 | Chelsea Players Rated In Disappointing Loss Vs Leeds United Chelsea welcomed Leeds United at Stamford Bridge earlier today as they hoped to secure a good result at home in the Premier League. The Blues made a decent start to the game and scored the opener in the 25th minute when Emmanuel Emegha found the back of the net. Noah Okafor equalised for Leeds just three minutes later as the two teams went into the half-time break with a 1-1 scoreline. Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored from the penalty spot in the 53rd minute before Okafor scored again just five minutes later. Brenden Aaronson scored another goal in injury time as the match ended with Xabi Alonso’s men suffering a disappointing 4-1 loss in front of their home fans. Let’s take a look at how each Chelsea player fared during the clash against the Whites. GK: Emiliano Martinez – 6/10 He made a few solid saves at the back but conceded four times this afternoon. RB: Josh Acheampong – 5.5/10 Acheampong did his fair share of defending but made a costly error at the back. CB: Wesley Fofana – 6.5/10 He made a lot of crucial clearances on the defensive end of the field. CB: Levi Colwill – 6/10 Colwill cleared his lines when he could and was strong in the air. LONDON, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 21: Jordan Henderson of Chelsea reacts after Noah Okafor of Leeds United scores his team’s third goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on November 21, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Jasper Wax/Getty Images) LB: Pep Chavarria – 6/10 He made two important clearances inside his half but failed to keep things solid defensively. CM: Romeo Lavia – 7/10 Lavia came back to defend when he could, but it was not enough today. He began the game well but had to be replaced in the 21st minute. RW: Estevao – 6.5/10 Estevao caught the eye at times on the right flank, but didn’t do enough to register a goal. CAM: Cole Palmer – 6/10 He managed to shine at times but failed to get his name on the scoresheet. LW: Morgan Rogers – 6.5/10 Rogers was a constant menace in the final third but gave away a cheap penalty. He has an assist to his name. ST: Emmanuel Emegha – 7/10 He took his goal well in the first half but was quiet in the second. CM: Jordan Henderson – 6/10 Henderson failed to impress during his time on the field. ST: Danny Welbeck – 6/10 He never looked like he would score. RM: Pedro Neto – 6/10 Neto made two decent chances in the final third. LW: Geovany Quenda – 6/10 He made one good chance up top.
