item.title: Fabregas on Jacobo Ramón: ‘He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker’
item.description: Fabregas on Jacobo Ramón: ‘He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker’ Cesc Fabregas praised Jacobo Ramón’s attacking threat after the defender scored in Como’s 2-0 win over Cagliari, although he insisted the performance was far from perfect. With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb , Ramón headed Como in front from Yan Couto’s assist in the 24th minute, and Lucas Da Cunha added a second, also set up by Couto, early in the second half. The win takes Fabregas’ side up to fourth for now, and Como remain unbeaten at the Sinigaglia in Serie A this season. “Perfect? No. We conceded four counter-attacks, three of them big chances where they could have scored,” Fabregas said. “They did something different going forward and found space in behind us, but from around the 35th minute things changed, and in the second half there was only one team on the pitch. “I’m very happy for the lads. There was so much energy, and Lahdo came on very well. We had to finish with two right-backs because we don’t have the players. Today my only attacking option on the bench was Nico Paz.” TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Jacobo Ramon of Como 1907 celebrates his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between Torino FC and Como 1907 at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on October 27, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Fàbregas on Ramón and Da Cunha Ramón has just been called up by Spain for the first time , and Fabregas believes his scoring has improved a lot. “There are players who are stronger, but he’s a player I like. I won’t say too much about how I feel about him, because he might read it later,” Fabregas joked. “We worked a lot on his finishing. Last year he couldn’t score in front of goal, even easy chances. Now he scores them. It shows you they’re kids, but they improve every year. “He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker, even when you don’t expect it, and he can play long and short. In the air, he’s first or second in Serie A for duels won. But if you want to reach the top, you have to handle Thuram and Esposito, so the lads understand they always have to do more to get to that level. “In five or six years, I’d like to see all these lads playing at World Cups and winning the Champions League. They have the chance to grow here.” ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Lucas Da Cunha of Como 1907 celebrates after scoring their team’s second goal during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and Cagliari Calcio at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Da Cunha started despite his efforts with France this week, because Maxence Caqueret picked up a minor problem on Friday. “Honestly, I wanted to rest him today, but we can’t take risks now, we’re down to 11, 12, 13 players. He’s a gem for us. He always raises the level. Today my only attacking option on the bench was Nico Paz.” TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Jacobo Ramon of Como 1907 celebrates his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between Torino FC and Como 1907 at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on October 27, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Fàbregas on Ramón and Da Cunha Ramón has just been called up by Spain for the first time , and Fabregas believes his scoring has improved a lot. “There are players who are stronger, but he’s a player I like. I won’t say too much about how I feel about him, because he might read it later,” Fabregas joked. “We worked a lot on his finishing. Last year he couldn’t score in front of goal, even easy chances. Now he scores them. It shows you they’re kids, but they improve every year. “He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker, even when you don’t expect it, and he can play long and short. In the air, he’s first or second in Serie A for duels won. But if you want to reach the top, you have to handle Thuram and Esposito, so the lads understand they always have to do more to get to that level. “In five or six years, I’d like to see all these lads playing at World Cups and winning the Champions League. They have the chance to grow here.” ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Lucas Da Cunha of Como 1907 celebrates after scoring their team’s second goal during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and Cagliari Calcio at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Da Cunha started despite his efforts with France this week, because Maxence Caqueret picked up a minor problem on Friday. “Honestly, I wanted to rest him today, but we can’t take risks now, we’re down to 11, 12, 13 players. He’s a gem for us. He always raises the level. I’d like every player in the world to have Da Cunha’s mentality.” He also warned there’s no room to ease off. “There are seven games left before Christmas, and everyone has to play their part.”

Former Baltimore Ravens safety Bernard Pollard has raised concerns about the organization’s fading defensive identity and Lamar Jackson ’s future amid trade speculation as the team prepares for its Week 11 road matchup against the Carolina Panthers. With the Ravens (4-6) looking to snap a five-game losing streak against the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, Pollard believes Baltimore has strayed from the defensive standard that defined the franchise for decades. They need to hold the players accountable to that, while bringing in players who hold each other accountable.” Baltimore’s defense has surrendered 2,306 passing yards and 1,059 rushing yards, including a league-high 14 rushing touchdowns. The unit has also allowed 12 receiving touchdowns and seven completions of at least 40 yards. With the Ravens (4-6) looking to snap a five-game losing streak against the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, Pollard believes Baltimore has strayed from the defensive standard that defined the franchise for decades. In a recent interview with Kyle Odegard of RotoGrinders, Pollard criticized the team’s defensive struggles and questioned whether its personnel and coaching staff have maintained that identity. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Some people may or may not like what I’m about to say, but they are losing the brand. The brand in Baltimore has always been defense. I don’t know if it’s a personnel thing or coaching, but you’ve got to get somebody in there who will keep that brand. They need to hold the players accountable to that, while bringing in players who hold each other accountable.” Baltimore’s defense has surrendered 2,306 passing yards and 1,059 rushing yards, including a league-high 14 rushing touchdowns. The unit has also allowed 12 receiving touchdowns and seven completions of at least 40 yards. The Ravens have surrendered more than 30 points in four of their 10 games, averaging 25.9 points allowed per contest. Baltimore’s struggles have intensified following Jackson’s latest injury. The two-time NFL MVP suffered a broken and dislocated right thumb during the Ravens’ 36-10 Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Bernard Pollard questions Lamar Jackson’s future with Ravens Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Pollard expressed concerns about Jackson’s durability as the quarterback approaches his 30th birthday. “With Lamar and the injury woes, Father Time is undefeated. He has been electric. He has been an exceptional talent running around and making plays with his legs, making plays with his arm. Jackson also holds a no-trade clause, meaning he would need to approve any potential move. item.title: Barcelona hit by Hamza Abdelkarim injury blow
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 03: Hamza Abdelkarim of FC Barcelona looks on prior to the UEFA Youth League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa FC at Estadi Johan Cruyff on November 03, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona have been hit by another injury blow as young striker Hamza Abdelkarim appears to have picked up a problem and been forced out of action. Abdelkarim was set to play for Barca Atletic in the derby clash against Espanyol on Saturday. He was named in Juliano Belletti’s injury-hit squad for the match but then dropped out unexpectedly at the last minute. Local reporter Achraf Ben Ayard has posted on X to say that Abdelkarim is “struggling with pain” which is why he is not able to play. However, there’s no futher detail on the nature of the actual problem. There was an expectation that Abdelkarim was also set to be part of the Barcelona first team squad to face Villarreal on Sunday but that now looks doubtful. Abdelkarim was in action over the international break, featuring as a substitute in Egypt’s two AFCON against Malawi, before returning to Barcelona.

item.title: ‘Are yall that addicted to a video game’: Stephen A. Smith ‘concerned’ about the effect GTA will have on athletes
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images. Rockstar Games. The biggest video game release this year is by far Grand Theft Auto VI . It’s been thirteen years since the latest release, and fans of all ages are enamored by the drop of their favorite childhood game. Recently, on The Stephen A. Smith Show, Smith commented on the game’s generational impact not only on the youth but also on some of today’s top athletes. Smith discussed the Miami Heat’s Grand Theft Auto VI–inspired “A Night in Vice City” crossover game in which they defeated the Milwaukee Bucks 137–130 on Wednesday. In a post-game interview, Miami center Bam Adebayo expressed his excitement for the game, stating he’d “absolutely” be taking part in gameplay later that evening. Before the game, newly acquired veteran guard Klay Thompson also chimed in on the affair, as he’s been a fan since the original Grand Theft Auto in the late 1990s. “I’ve been playing GTA since it was the Bird’s-eye view on the original PlayStation, and I’m just 36, but I’ll still be gaming when I get this version, and the story mode of this game is maybe the best in all of gaming. It will feel much better to have a day of gaming when we get that victory on Wednesday,” Thompson said . Thompson’s comments confused Smith, as he couldn’t comprehend how adults could be so invested in a fictional storyline. Wednesday, Cleveland Browns quarterback DeShaun Watson threw cold water on any playoff conversations for the team during their bye week due to GTA’s release. “Coach dont even mention it…we’re not getting ahead of ourselves must of those guys are thinking about GTA VI, for real,” Watson said. Disgusted by the barrage of GTA praise from professional athletes, Smith criticized them for their blatant disinterest in their jobs, “without shame,” calling it an “addiction to the game.” “At 6-4, nobody should be feeling comfortable enough to be sitting up there playing video games during the regular season, as far as I’m concerned, Smith added. Smith also mentioned that Houston Rockets center Steven Adams spoke about the anticipation of the game, warning the league to prepare for the date earlier this season. “You guys should anticipate November. The performance of the league, league-wide, guys will fake injuries; GTA is dropping,” Adams told CBS Sports in September . “So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though,” Adams added. “Most of the boys will get it done — hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.” Now, Smith has refuted his comments targeted at GTA enthusiasts on Wednesday and claimed to be “joking” in a response post to Heat Central on X . “False! I don’t think it’s a Major Problem,” Smith wrote Thursday. “I was just having fun asking

item.title: Jorge Martin on keeping MotoGP title hopes alive: ‘I didn’t do anything, it was in Marquez’s hands’
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin admitted that he lacked speed in the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint, suggesting he owes his slim MotoGP title hopes entirely to Marc Marquez ’s crash. The factory Aprilia rider arrived at Portimao needing to outscore Marquez by 24 points over the weekend to take the championship fight to the Valencia finale. But after qualifying five places behind Marquez in seventh, Martin failed to make any headway in the sprint, gaining only one position in the opening 10 laps. That would have let Marquez seal the title with a third-place finish, but the Ducati star crashed out of the sprint on the penultimate tour as rain began to fall on the track. Speaking afterwards, Martin admitted that he was lagging behind the frontrunners at Portimao, particularly with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi converting pole position into a dominant win. Asked whether he had kept his championship hopes alive, Martin insisted the outcome was never in his hands given the points situation. “Well, I didn't ‘keep’ anything. Everything was in Marc's hands,” he said. “For sure, it was a really tricky race. I didn't have the speed all weekend. Finally, in the race, it seemed I found a little bit extra. I was quite close to the podium fight, but I missed a bit more speed. “But in the end, I did my best. I finished in fifth position. Let's hope for a bigger improvement tomorrow. “When the conditions are really tricky like this, the focus more goes on riding because you need to be at 100%. “So you don't have room to think about anything. I was just really focused. I tried to fight the first few laps with Pedro [Acosta], trying to go in the front, and he was a bit faster. “We were catching the riders in front a bit, so this is good. I saw the places where I'm a bit slower, the places where I'm a bit faster than him.” Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Marquez has shown remarkable consistency since he returned from injury at the Italian Grand Prix in May, avoiding the kind of mistakes that have plagued Bezzecchi and Martin’s campaigns. The reigning world champion himself noted that his crash out of the sprint was his first real mistake in the second half of the season, coming just a day after he warned about the risks of racing with the title within reach. Martin said he understood why Marquez made an error at such a crucial stage of the championship, particularly with the weather conditions changing at Portimao. “Surprised? No. In these tricky conditions, anything can happen. “When you are in front, I can understand his position. Everything gets more risky, everything gets more stiff, as he said yesterday. “The problem for him was he wasn't alone at that point. I was behind Marc and Alex [Marquez]. So I saw the crash and then I relaxed a bit in that corner. Otherwise, maybe I would [also] crash. “So, this is racing and a bit unlucky. I thought he was going to make it [win the championship], honestly. So it was incredible. “I have another chance tomorrow, but anyway

item.title: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win
item.description: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win Celtic’s midfield required some personnel changes this afternoon, with both Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur ruled out through injury. That presented an opportunity for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan, and they seized their chance to great effect, both of them getting on the scoresheet in the 4-1 victory over St Mirren and make a good contribution to the overall performance and result Indeed, Oxlade-Chamberlain, who opened the scoring just after the half-hour mark, was also given the Man of the Match award for his contribution. Both players spoke to CelticPlayer after the game, and the England internationalist said: “I thought in the first half we were pretty good,” he said. “We played some really nice stuff with the ball. “We defended pretty well throughout the half, and being clinical when you get the chances is massive. "Today we were able to do that. That obviously sets you up to be able to try and control the game a bit more. “In the second half, St Mirren played some really good stuff, to be fair to them, and had moments where they controlled it, but the lead that we gave ourselves in the first half made it a bit more comfortable from there.” And Luke McCowan was also delighted to play his part in the win over St Mirren, which saw him score Celtic’s third goal just before the break. He said: “It felt great. I worked hard to keep myself in the position almost, but I was just happy to be back out there playing. “As he (Alex) says, being clinical really helps. Obviously, in past situations here, we've probably not been as clinical, but today we were, and it helps us control the game." Fixtures Celtic Vs. St. Mirren - Sat, Nov 21st 2026, 15:00

item.title: UFC Qatar Highlights! Amir Albazi Scores Comeback Choke For First Win In Three Years
item.description: DOHA, QATAR - NOVEMBER 21: Amir Albazi of Iraq reacts after a submission victory against Alessandro Costa of Brazil in a flyweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at ABHA Arena on November 21, 2026 in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Amir Albazi re-entered the flyweight win column earlier today (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) at UFC Qatar LIVE on Paramount+ from inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar, as the perennial contender ended Brazilian Alessandro Costa with a third-round submission (rear-naked choke). This fight was a tale of two rounds. Albazi dominated the first round by using his grappling and landing countless punches without answer. Costa is tough, though, so he was able to battle back in the second round and nearly finished Albazi with a barrage of strikes and a ton of takedowns. Albazi somehow survived, but the round was a massive momentum swing in favor of Costa. Albazi, who may have needed a finish in the third round to avoid a potential draw, let everything go in the final minutes of the fight. The Iraqi fighter was able to get the fight to the ground once again and found a way to get to Costa’s back. Albazi sunk in the tight rear-naked choke, forced Costa to tap, and walked off with his first win since a split-decision over Kai Kara-France back in June 2023. item.title: Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them
item.description: Jul 22, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; former Alabama Crimson Tide coach and ESPN analyst for College GameDay Nick Saban broadcast during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images With just a couple of weeks left in the regular season, the College Football Playoff picture is starting to come into focus. And one of the most decorated coaches in the sport’s history thinks that only a few teams have what it takes to win it all. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban said on Friday that there are “three teams that have the right stuff” to win the national championship: Georgia, Utah, and Notre Dame. And despite spending more than two decades coaching in the SEC, he made sure to clarify that it was “no disrespect to Alabama.” Playoff Picture Taking Shape Georgia sits at No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings at 9-1, with its only loss coming against Auburn in October. The Bulldogs have won three straight since then, including a 48-21 win over Missouri last weekend. Utah is right behind at No. 2 and is one of two undefeated teams in the top five at 10-0, along with No. 4 UCLA, though the Utes needed a 40-39 win at Arizona last weekend to keep their perfect season alive. Notre Dame checks in at No. 6 at 9-1, with its only loss coming at BYU. The Fighting Irish have since won three straight, including a 31-24 win over Miami. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr were both named finalists for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award on Friday, according to On3. On the same show, Saban insisted that the SEC is still the best conference from top to bottom, despite the Big Ten winning three straight national titles. Yet only one of his three contenders plays in the SEC. ‘The right stuff’ Saban shared his picks during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think there’s three teams that have the right stuff. And this is no disrespect to Alabama, because I think there’s probably seven to eight teams that can win the championship, Alabama being one of them. But if you’re a betting man and you say, ‘OK, who can run the ball, who can play good defense and who has a good quarterback?’ You would say Georgia has that, Utah has that, Notre Dame has that,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban added that the rest of the contenders have weaknesses that could hold them back. “Everybody else maybe has a flaw somewhere along the way. Now they might be able to overcome it, but I think those three teams have the right stuff,” Saban said. That leaves out Alabama, which the committee has ranked No. 3, as well as No. 4 UCLA, No. 5 Texas, and No. 7 Miami, among others. Clearly, Saban thinks the national title race is a lot narrower than the rankings suggest. The post Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield considered ‘good to go’ in latest injury update, but there’s a catch
item.description: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield considered ‘good to go’ in latest injury update, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Although it is not guaranteed to happen, Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is on track to return for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions, per Tom Pelissero of NFL Network. Pelissero revealed why his return isn’t guaranteed yet, however. “Barring a setback, Baker Mayfield is good to go Sunday against the Lions. He is expected to wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help with the injury,” Pelissero wrote. The Buccaneers are obviously proceeding with caution. If any setbacks occur, Tampa Bay likely won’t hesitate to give the QB another week of rest. Mayfield, who is battling a plantar fascia injury , will play on Sunday if no setbacks occur, though. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bucs would love to have Mayfield available . The 31-year-old has had an up and down campaign, but he is capable of leading the team to victory in any given contest. Still, his numbers aren’t pretty across his six games played this season. Mayfield has thrown for 922 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions. He also has 80 rushing yards and one touchdown on the ground. Tampa Bay happens to play in a weak NFC South, so the team is still in the conversation to win the division. At 3-6, they are tied for second place with the New Orleans Saints. The 4-5 Carolina Panthers currently lead the division. Baker Mayfield will look to overcome his injury concern and lead the Buccaneers to the postseason. Updates on his injury status will continue to be monitored and provided as they are made available. item.title: UFC Qatar live results, highlights, play-by-play | Prochazka vs. Stirling
item.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live THIS MORNING (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) with UFC Qatar , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event takes place inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Our main event for this early morning card is Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling in UFC’s Light Heavyweight division. UFC Qatar Preview UFC is closing out 2026 with a Middle East swing and then a home game at T-Mobile Arena. The first of those Middle East shows is this weekend in Doha, Qatar. This the promotion’s second time in Qatar, following the Arman Tsarukyan vs. Dan Hooker -led card we had last year. This time there’s two potential title eliminator bouts on tap in the desert. The main event could generate the next opponent for recovering UFC Light Heavyweight champion, Carlos Ulberg ( those details here ). That fight pits his last opponent, Jiri Prochazka , against his City Kickboxing teammate, Navajo Stirling . Prochazka hasn’t competed since Ulberg knocked him out on one leg ( re-live that here ). Stirling is getting a relatively short turnaround after KOing Jan Blachowicz in August ( watch it ). The co-main is Aljamain Sterling vs. Kevin Vallejos . Sterling just took out a rising prospect in the form of Youssef Zalal , and now he’ll try and do that again. Vallejos comes in here after starching Josh Emmett . The winner of this one might end up in a Featherweight title fight, especially if Alexander Volkanovski vacates the belt so he can chase Lightweight gold. Dan Hooker is back in Qatar this weekend. He’s welcoming Brian Ortega to the Lightweight division. The main card also has Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev in a key Flyweight bout. Jared Cannonier vs. Ikram Aliskerov rounds out the card. The featured “Prelims” bout is Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna . The shorter than usual card also has Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira , Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa 2, Jake Matthews vs. Tahir Abdullayev , Niklos Motta vs. Dom Mar Fan , Diyar Nurgozhay vs. Alik Lorenzb and Shoaib Yousaf vs. John Mitchell. UFC Qatar Start Date and Time We’re watching fights over coffee this morning, if you are in on US east coast time like me. Here are the times for each portion of today’s UFC Qatar card: UFC Qatar “Prelims” will begin at 1o a.m. ET . UFC Qatar main card is scheduled to start at 1 p.m. ET . All of UFC Qatar airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here . The live blog here starts rolling below at 10 a.m. ET . Come in and say hi! UFC QATAR QUICK RESULTS Main card 205 lbs.: Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling 145 lbs.: Aljamain Sterling vs. Kevin Vallejos 155 lbs.: Dan Hooker vs. Brian Ortega 125 lbs.: Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev 185 lbs.: Jared Cannonier vs. Ikram Aliskerov Prelims 135 lbs.: Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna 265 lbs.: Tallison Teixeira def. Shamil Gaziev by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28) 125 lbs.: Amir Albazi def. Alessandro Costa by submission (rear naked choke), round 3 (4:34) — HIGHLIGHTS 170 lbs.: Tahir Abdullay

UFC QATAR QUICK RESULTS Main card 205 lbs.: Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling 145 lbs.: Aljamain Sterling vs. Kevin Vallejos 155 lbs.: Dan Hooker vs. Brian Ortega 125 lbs.: Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev 185 lbs.: Jared Cannonier vs. Ikram Aliskerov Prelims 135 lbs.: Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna 265 lbs.: Tallison Teixeira def. Shamil Gaziev by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28) 125 lbs.: Amir Albazi def. Alessandro Costa by submission (rear naked choke), round 3 (4:34) — HIGHLIGHTS 170 lbs.: Tahir Abdullayev def. Jake Matthews by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) 155 lbs.: Dom Mar Fan def. Nikolas Motta by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 29-27) 205 lbs.: Diyar Nurgozhay def. Alik Lorenz by TKO (head kick and punches), round 2 (0:24) — HIGHLIGHTS 155 lbs.: John Mitchell def. Shoaib Yousaf by KO (knee and punches), round 1 (3:50) – HIGHLIGHTS UFC QATAR PLAY-BY-PLAY UPDATES Prelims Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna: Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira: That was one of those terrible heavyweight fights we get served up every now and then. Very little happened here and neither guy deserved a W on their record. I thought Gaziev did marginally more and should have gotten the decision, but it’s hard to get mad when the fight is that bad. Official decision: Tallison Teixeira def. Shamil Gaziev by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28) Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa: Albazi showed a ton of grit in this one. He took the first round on Costa and was almost finished in the second. He was docked a point for a fence grab in the second, while he survived Costa’s attempt to hunt for a finish. In the second Albazi’s wrestling took over again and we were on course for a draw until Albazi snatched up a rear naked choke. He’s now 2-0 against Costa. 2/2 ✅ Amir Albazi wins the rematch against Alessandro Costa by submission at #UFCQatar [ LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/FRZvft7faX — UFC (@ufc) November 21, 2026 Official decision: Amir Albazi def. Alessandro Costa by submission (rear naked choke), round 3 (4:34) Jake Matthews vs. Tahir Abdullayev: Abdullayev hurt Matthews on the feet in the first round and then spent much of the second and third laying on top of him. Matthews fell in love with going for submissions off his back. But his gogoplata and triangle attempts weren’t close to finishing Abdullayev and they didn’t win him any scorecards either. They also let the tried Abdullayev spend a lot more time on top, while not producing much offense. Official decision: Tahir Abdullayev def. Jake Matthews by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) Dom Mar Fan vs. Nikolas Motta: Dom Mar Fan rearranged Nikolas Motta’s face. He took him down in the second and caused a ton of damage with ground and pound. Motta responded with a knockdown in the second round, but Fan used his grappling to survive. These two traded a bunch on the feet after that and Fan landed some massive shots that opened up all kinds of cuts on Motta’s poor face. Official decision: Dom Mar Fan def. Nikolas Motta by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 29-27) Diyar Nurgozhay vs. Alik Lorenz: Nurgozhay and Lorenz had a fun back and forth brawl in the first round. Nurgozhay looked like the more polished and UFC ready product, though. In the second Nugozhay sliced Lorenz with a head kick and then put him away with punches. THIS HEAD KICK 😮‍💨 Diyar Nurgozhay gets his third win in a row in the UFC [ #UFCQatar | LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/bqsEswwOFd — UFC (@ufc) November 21, 2026 Official decision: Diyar Nurgozhay def. Alik Lorenz by TKO (head kick and punches), round 2 (0:24) John Mitchell vs. Shoaib Yousaf: The hastily put together battle of journeymen finished in the first round. The commentary team was loving on Shoaib Yousaf, but the better tested John Mitchell patiently went about his work and eventually put Yousaf down with a big knee and follow up punches. Answered the call 🙌 John Mitchell makes the most of his short-notice debut! [ LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/7Ap1ViRJni — UFC (@ufc) November 21, 2026 Official decision: John Mitchell def. Shoaib Yousaf by KO (knee and punches), round 1 (3:50) Live stream begins at 10 p.m. ET. … For more UFC Qatar: “Prochazka vs. Stirling” news and notes be sure to hit up our comprehensive event archive right here .

item.title: Championship roundup: Middlesbrough hit top spot; 10-man Stoke go second
item.description: Boro beat Bristol City 2-0; Stoke 1-0 Birmingham Scott Parker still winless as West Ham held by Preston Middlesbrough scored a goal either side of half-time to climb to the top of the Championship with a 2-0 win that piled further pressure on the Bristol City manager Michael Skubala. Adilson Malanda’s header five minutes before half-time was followed by David Strelec’s finish in the 54th minute to secure a Boro victory. The three points were effectively secured before Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg introduced the division’s top scorer, Will Lankshear, for the final 14 minutes from the bench after injury. Defeat heightened the frustrations being felt by the Robins, who have won just one of their last eight matches, as they dropped down to 18th. Continue reading...

item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was a triumph of sorts. The hard numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the Sunderland box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable too. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the only survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic just seven months ago. With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving one of Zion Suzuki’s uprights with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka and comfortably eliminating the defender before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to a post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches. Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. The post Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

item.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
item.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. item.title: Man City stumble against Fulham; Leeds thrash Chelsea at Stamford Bridge
item.description: Manchester City’s winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday, as Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City’s title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules. The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal. After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca’s reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City’s quest to topple defending champions Arsenal. Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz. The home side were furious that Erling Haaland’s equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno. Elliot Anderson’s sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display. “Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it’s for sure something we need to improve,” said Maresca. Leeds humble Chelsea Leeds climbed into the top six after coming from behind to stun Chelsea. Emmanuel Emegha’s first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny. Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot. Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals. Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games. Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign. Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men. Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table. Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half. Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone. item.title: FBI criminal database hacked
item.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027 Elections: Tinubu Endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Tinubu endorsed the candidates on Saturday by raising their hands at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State. Introducing the candidates, the President told supporters, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State. He subsequently raised the hands of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the party’s candidate in Ogun State, and Obafemi Hamzat, its governorship candidate in Lagos State. Tinubu also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South, by raising his hand at the rally. ﻿ The event marked the South-West leg of the President’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally. Tinubu, who arrived in Ibadan alongside his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said he was in the state to appreciate residents for their support during the 2023 presidential election. He expressed confidence that they would vote for the APC again in 2027. “I am just here to say thank you for standing with us. You gave us votes in 2023, and I am sure you will do the same in 2027,” he said. The President, however, kept his speech brief and asked the audience to observe a minute’s silence in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday. Tinubu had earlier directed that the Ibadan rally be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died in the incident and in sympathy with their families. He also disclosed that he had met with traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, expressing confidence in their support. The President further promised improved electricity supply and industrial development, announcing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan for the assembly of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. “We will bring industries and provide jobs for our youths,” he said. The APC is seeking to take control of Oyo State from the incumbent administration of Governor Seyi Makinde, while Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, emerged as the party’s consensus governorship candidate in May. In Ogun State, Adeola, who represents Ogun West Senatorial District, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is flying the party’s flag in the 2027 governorship election. The endorsements placed the three governorship contests alongside Tinubu’s re-election campaign as the APC seeks to

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But when the momentum is against you, sometimes even a change of manager cannot stop the rot. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. Palace may feel themselves unlucky, but Thomas Frank started with a defeat and his side have now lost five successive league games. For much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour for a win that lifted them three points clear of the relegation zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Tinubu’s achievements will give him victory in Edo – Shaibu
item.description: .Says Obi’s 2023 wave won’t repeat itself ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ABUJA – FORMER Deputy Governor of Edo State and Director-General/CEO of National Institute for Sports, NIS, Rt. Hon. Philip Shaibu has said that the political wave that gave victory to the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, in 2023 election in the state, Mr. Peter Obi, will not repeat itself in the 2027 polls. ‎Shaibu said President Bola Tinubu’s reforms and achievements would give victory. ‎Speaking exclusively to Sunday Vanguard, Shaibu, who was a former President of National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, said no elections can be the same. “From my experience so far in Nigerian politics—I have actively participated since 2023, beyond student union government elections and the politics of activism—my political career started mainly in 2023 in Edo State. “Since then, from my little experience in active partisan politics, I know that no two elections are the same. Every election has its own dynamics, its own spirit, and its own issues that drive it. Edo is not different from the cyclical politics played in Nigeria. ‎”The 2023 election was a wave that we had never experienced in this country. That wave occurred because young Nigerians were interested in who became their president, and they were looking for an alternative. ‎”Even when the alternative they later got was not fully known to them, they simply wanted an alternative—someone they seemingly believed could be it, even though they did not have much information. ‎”They were persuaded and mobilised through the power of social media. Do not forget that the EndSARS protests created room for all that happened in 2023. ‎”But 2027 is a different ballgame. First, Asiwaju (President Tinubu) is now known to the people. He is known by the young people in this country, not only by partisan politicians in the state. He has now been president for over three years, and people understand what governance is. ‎”The person they thought was going to be a messiah—they have started seeing that he has more than one shoe that he claims to have. They have started seeing that the empire he has built is more than somebody owning a shoe. ‎”They have seen that the statistics they were reading, those statistics are all fallacy, they were all wrong. They were one of those home video acting to just convince people, but because people did not take time to check and that was why that wave. ‎”That wave cannot return in the next election, because even the young men and women—when you see the Tinubu support groups, you will see that it is dominated by these same young people who were part of that wave. ‎”So the politics of 2027 will be completely different from the politics of 2023, because we now know who President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is. We now know who the other opponents are. We have opponents, but we do not have an opposition. I can tell you that for the 2027 election, there are opponents, but there is no opposition.” ‎Asked why he said that
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: .Says Obi’s 2023 wave won’t repeat itself ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ABUJA – FORMER Deputy Governor of Edo State and Director-General/CEO of National Institute for Sports, NIS, Rt. Hon. Philip Shaibu has said that the political wave that gave victory to the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, in 2023 election in the state, Mr. Peter Obi, will not repeat itself in the 2027 polls. ‎Shaibu said President Bola Tinubu’s reforms and achievements would give victory. ‎Speaking exclusively to Sunday Vanguard, Shaibu, who was a former President of National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, said no elections can be the same. “From my experience so far in Nigerian politics—I have actively participated since 2023, beyond student union government elections and the politics of activism—my political career started mainly in 2023 in Edo State. “Since then, from my little experience in active partisan politics, I know that no two elections are the same. Every election has its own dynamics, its own spirit, and its own issues that drive it. Edo is not different from the cyclical politics played in Nigeria. ‎”The 2023 election was a wave that we had never experienced in this country. That wave occurred because young Nigerians were interested in who became their president, and they were looking for an alternative. ‎”Even when the alternative they later got was not fully known to them, they simply wanted an alternative—someone they seemingly believed could be it, even though they did not have much information. ‎”They were persuaded and mobilised through the power of social media. Do not forget that the EndSARS protests created room for all that happened in 2023. ‎”But 2027 is a different ballgame. First, Asiwaju (President Tinubu) is now known to the people. He is known by the young people in this country, not only by partisan politicians in the state. He has now been president for over three years, and people understand what governance is. ‎”The person they thought was going to be a messiah—they have started seeing that he has more than one shoe that he claims to have. They have started seeing that the empire he has built is more than somebody owning a shoe. ‎”They have seen that the statistics they were reading, those statistics are all fallacy, they were all wrong. They were one of those home video acting to just convince people, but because people did not take time to check and that was why that wave. ‎”That wave cannot return in the next election, because even the young men and women—when you see the Tinubu support groups, you will see that it is dominated by these same young people who were part of that wave. ‎”So the politics of 2027 will be completely different from the politics of 2023, because we now know who President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is. We now know who the other opponents are. We have opponents, but we do not have an opposition. I can tell you that for the 2027 election, there are opponents, but there is no opposition.” ‎Asked why he said that there were opponents and no opposition, Shaibu said: “There are opponents who just need their names to appear on the ballot. ‎”When you have an opposition, you have a presidential candidate who carries weight and is a threat in every unit, in every ward, across the country. But what we have now are candidates who want their names on the ballot paper, yet already know they are only popular in a particular catchment area of the country. ‎”But we have a president who is known, who has agents and representatives in every unit in Nigeria, and that person is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The other candidates do not have that spread. So we have candidates, but no opposition. We have aspirants, but they are not an opposition. Unlike 2023, when we had both opposition and aspirants, in 2027 we only have aspirants. “Do not forget that it is only in this country that people struggle to become aspirants so that, after the election, they can have a complementary title as a former presidential aspirant or former gubernatorial aspirant.” ‎ ‎ The post Tinubu’s achievements will give him victory in Edo – Shaibu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich
item.description: Not since the emergence of Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and matchwinning assist against Ipswich. That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. Continue reading...

item.title: How to use auto drive in GTA 6
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 's auto drive feature is perfect if you just want to see the sights of Leonida or avoid navigating through traffic. Not that GTA 6 goes out of its way to tell you there even is an auto drive feature. It's tucked away in a menu you have little cause to use early in the game, and you also need to make sure a specific setting is toggled on for it to work in some circumstances. It's best to still learn how to drive decently yourself, though, as auto drive isn't the best choice in hectic situations.

item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Adeola Badru President Bola Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Tinubu, who spoke at the APC presidential campaign rally held at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday, called on the electorate to remain steadfast in their support for the party, while promising increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply. The President also endorsed Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in Oyo State, urging the electorate to vote for him in the forthcoming election. He said the people of Oyo State had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election and should not abandon the party, stressing that their continued backing would help secure a better future for their children and generations yet unborn. The rally was preceded by the arrival of the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, where the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and other members of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs received him. Addressing the political gathering at Mapo Hall, Tinubu called on the electorate to sustain their loyalty to the APC, describing the party as their own political platform. “I just want to say thank you. Thank you for all you have been doing and all the support you have given to APC. APC is our party. It’s your party. Is it clear?” he said. The President reminded the electorate that they had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election, urging them to remain committed to the party as the country prepares for another general election. “You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” the president said. He stressed that the decisions being taken by the present generation must create opportunities for future generations to benefit from the country’s development. “Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria,” the President said. He added that the country must prioritise education and agriculture to ensure that younger generations had the opportunity to thrive. “We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said. Bayelsa boat accident victims Before addressing the political gathering, Tinubu called for a minute’s silence in honour of those who lost their lives in a boat accident in Bayelsa State. The President expressed sympathy with the bereaved families and the people of the state, assuring them of the nation’s solidarity during their period of grief. “To show respect and appreciate those who lost their lives when the boat capsized in Bayelsa State. We show solidarity and sympathy. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. And we have one minute of silence,” he said. The President also announced that his administration had signed an agreement with a Chinese company, U-Turn, to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, describing the initiative as part of efforts to revive industrial activities in Oyo State. Tinubu said the factory would be reopened for the production of public transport vehicles and the establishment of automobile assembly plants, promising that his administration would continue to attract industries to the state. “For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added. The announcement was also welcomed by Olubadan, who expressed appreciation to the President for infrastructure projects being undertaken across the country, particularly in the South-West. The monarch specifically mentioned the Leyland Motor Assembly in Ibadan, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road, saying the projects would help address longstanding infrastructure challenges. Tinubu also assured the people of Oyo State that electricity supply would improve, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team. “You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team.” Tinubu also used the occasion to recognise the contributions of APC elders and leaders, particularly those who had continued to support the party over the years. He specifically mentioned former Ogun State Governor, Aremo Olusegun Osoba, and former Osun State Governor, Chief Bisi Akande, commending them and other party elders for their commitment to the APC. “Now it is time to say thank you to all the elders, starting from Aremo Olusegun Osoba, Chief Bisi Akande, and others who have been holding the flag and supporting the party ever since. I salute sincerely,” he said. The President also acknowledged traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, saying he had seen and spoken with them. “I salute Olubadan. I’ve seen him. Soun of Ogbomosho and all the other obas. I’ve spoken with them. They will support you in every way possible,” he said. He expressed confidence that the traditional rulers would continue to support the APC, saying he had interacted with them and believed they would assist the party in every way possible. The President, however, took a swipe at opposition parties, dismissing their capacity and urging the electorate not to be distracted by them. “And there is a party around that cannot hold anything, please don’t look at them, they are mediocre,” he said. Tinubu subsequently declared his support for Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in Oyo State, urging the electorate to vote for him in the 2027 election. “I will show you the governorship candidate in Oyo State that you must vote for, and is Sen. Sharafadeen Alli,” the President said. Olubadan Earlier, the President was received at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and scores of monarchs drawn from the various traditional councils across Oyo State. The monarchs, who arrived at the airport at about 1.30pm, were drawn from Ibadan, Ibarapa, Oyo, Ogbomoso and Oke-Ogun zones I and II. Their presence was to reaffirm the position of leading South-West monarchs at their recent meeting in Ibadan on Tinubu’s re-election. Welcoming the President and his entourage on behalf of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs, the Olubadan, who is also the chairman of the council, described Tinubu as the leader the monarchs had been waiting to receive. “This is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu that we have been waiting for,” the Olubadan said. The monarch contended that, just as a man’s gifts could make a way for him, so could the work of his hands. He appreciated the President for the infrastructure development projects being undertaken nationwide, particularly in the South-West, describing them as works in progress. Olubadan said the projects should be completed before fresh requests were made for additional ones. He expressed gratitude to Tinubu for the Leyland Motor Assembly project in Ibadan, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road, among others. According to him, many of the roads had previously fallen into a terrible state of disrepair, exposing commuters to untold suffering. In his remarks, Tinubu thanked the monarchs for their prayers and co-operation, urging them to prevail on their subjects to come out en masse and vote in the forthcoming election. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
item.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

item.title: Where to find the bowling alley safe code in GTA 6
item.description: The Kingpin Bowling Alley safe code in Grand Theft Auto 6 is, frustratingly, not actually in the bowling alley itself. No, to get your hands on it legitimately, you need to ransack a different Kolt & Associates illegal operation, which essentially acts as the gang's headquarters, and has multiple safe codes available at once. But that doesn't help when you're deep in the back offices of the bowling alley, and you're being shot at by dozens of angry gang members.

item.title: ‘I Guarantee You Improvement In Electricity,’ Tinubu Tells Nigerians At Oyo Presidential Campaign Rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges. The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We will continue to bring industry, you will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team. You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time; you must stay the course for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for the children and our great-grandchildren. Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in Agriculture,” he said. ﻿ The President also announced plans to revive the defunct Leyland automobile factory in Ibadan through an agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong. “For Oyo State, we have signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant there,” he said. The agreement, signed on November 19, 2026, involves the Federal Government, through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong and its local partner, YP Automobile. Electricity Challenges A depiction of a lantern and grid Tinubu’s latest assurance comes amid growing frustration among Nigerians over inadequate electricity supply, with households and businesses grappling with prolonged outages in different parts of the country. The shortages have renewed questions about the effectiveness of the Band A, B and C electricity tariff classification, which links customers’ payments to the minimum hours of electricity supply they are expected to receive. Customers on Band A, who are entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, have also complained about inadequate supply. Intense heat has compounded the situation, leaving many residents struggling to cope without electricity to run fans and air conditioners. Several Nigerians, including figures like Kate Henshaw and Cute Abiola, have expressed frustration over persistent power outages, lamenting that households have become “mini-factories” forced to generate their own electricity. Meanwhile, rising petrol and diesel prices have made generator use increasingly expensive, while the cost of installing solar panels, batteries and inverters remains beyond the reach of many households and small businesses. Minister of Power Tegbe recently attributed the prolonged blackouts to planned maintenance at the Egbin Power Station, gas supply shortages and vandalism of transmission infrastructure. A general view of a solar energy recharging box where mobile phone batteries are recharged with solar for customers, in Ogbabo village Doma, Nassarawa State, Nigeria on October 16, 2023. (Photo by Kola Sulaimon / AFP) Tin

item.content:encoded: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges. The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We will continue to bring industry, you will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team. You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time; you must stay the course for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for the children and our great-grandchildren. Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in Agriculture,” he said. ﻿ The President also announced plans to revive the defunct Leyland automobile factory in Ibadan through an agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong. “For Oyo State, we have signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant there,” he said. The agreement, signed on November 19, 2026, involves the Federal Government, through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong and its local partner, YP Automobile. Electricity Challenges A depiction of a lantern and grid Tinubu’s latest assurance comes amid growing frustration among Nigerians over inadequate electricity supply, with households and businesses grappling with prolonged outages in different parts of the country. The shortages have renewed questions about the effectiveness of the Band A, B and C electricity tariff classification, which links customers’ payments to the minimum hours of electricity supply they are expected to receive. Customers on Band A, who are entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, have also complained about inadequate supply. Intense heat has compounded the situation, leaving many residents struggling to cope without electricity to run fans and air conditioners. Several Nigerians, including figures like Kate Henshaw and Cute Abiola, have expressed frustration over persistent power outages, lamenting that households have become “mini-factories” forced to generate their own electricity. Meanwhile, rising petrol and diesel prices have made generator use increasingly expensive, while the cost of installing solar panels, batteries and inverters remains beyond the reach of many households and small businesses. Minister of Power Tegbe recently attributed the prolonged blackouts to planned maintenance at the Egbin Power Station, gas supply shortages and vandalism of transmission infrastructure. A general view of a solar energy recharging box where mobile phone batteries are recharged with solar for customers, in Ogbabo village Doma, Nassarawa State, Nigeria on October 16, 2023. (Photo by Kola Sulaimon / AFP) Tinubu’s 2023 Electricity Promise The President’s latest assurance has also brought renewed attention to his 2023 campaign promise to tackle Nigeria’s electricity challenges and end estimated billing. During his campaign, Tinubu told members of the Organised Private Sector in Lagos that Nigerians should hold him accountable if he failed to deliver on the promise. “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver,” he said. The pledge returned to public discussion this week following comments by former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola, during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Fashola argued that Tinubu did not specifically promise Nigerians 24-hour electricity during the 2023 campaign, saying his remarks had been taken out of context. He explained that the President’s statement contained a qualification that voters should not re-elect him if he failed to deliver, unless he provided adequate reasons for the failure. Fashola also urged Nigerians to assess the administration’s performance based on their personal experiences with electricity supply and the progress made in ending estimated billing. His comments, however, attracted criticism from opposition figures and the campaign organisation of Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, who argued that the debate over the wording of Tinubu’s promise did not address the continuing power challenges facing Nigerians. item.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
item.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

item.title: D&D Publisher Officially Hands Record-Breaking AI Settlement Money to Authors
item.description: Anthropic, known for creating the AI platform Claude , was the target of a 2025 class-action lawsuit that resulted in the largest copyright settlement to date. While it was determined that Anthropic could use fairly obtained books to train large language models (LLMs) for Claude, the company resorted to using pirate libraries with thousands of unauthorized copies. This was later deemed an unfair use of authors' copyrighted work. Anthropic agreed to a settlement of $1.5 billion to be distributed among the publishers and authors of approximately half a million books.
